name: Ingush
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: Nearly every Ingush simplex word has a tonic syllable, and in nearly all Ingush words the tonic syllable is the initial syllable. Phonetically, stress is marked by greater prominence and the capacity to bear phrasal accent; a word pronounced in isolation has primary phrasal accent on its stressed syllable, which is therefore higher in pitch than the rest.

tone_statements.citation: Borise, Lena. 2021. Word Stress in Languages of the Caucasus. In Maria Polinsky (ed.), The Oxford Handbook of Languages of the Caucasus, 729-755. Oxford: Oxford University Press. doi:10.1093/oxfordhb/9780190690694.013.19. [Author preprint: 'Word Stress in the Languages of the Caucasus', draft November 2018, 33 pp., lingbuzz/004203]
tone_statements.quote: Closely related Ingush also has stress fixed on the first syllable. Exceptions to this include certain causative forms of the verb, in which the causative suffix attracts stress away from the initial syllable, and disyllabic teen numerals (Nichols 2011: 100). Chechen and Ingush have also been analyzed as having some tonal distinctions, which are only found on a small number of discourse particles (Nichols 1994: 44; Nichols 1997: 942); more on this in Borise-tone (this volume) and Komen et al. (this volume).
tone_statements.locator: preprint p. 6 (sec. 3 'Fixed-stress languages', Chechen/Ingush paragraph) and p. 11 (sec. 5.2, stress-attracting negative/prohibitive morphemes); published version pp. 729-755
tone_statements.summary: Fixed word-initial stress (few morphological exceptions) plus a marginal high tone restricted to a small closed set of grammatical particles/clitics.

tone_statements.citation: Ingush Language Project (UC Berkeley; PI Johanna Nichols). n.d. [c. 2000]. The Scientific Interest of Ingush, section 3: Tone system (unpublished draft, supported by NSF grant 96-16448). Web page, University of California, Berkeley, Department of Linguistics.
tone_statements.quote: In Ingush a handful of morphemes (all of them grammatical formatives) carry a tone realized as a high fall on the tone-bearing morpheme or (if it is enclitic) on the preceding syllable (even if that is an epenthetic schwa). Historically, this tone may have been non-initial stress; but now stress in Ingush is invariably word-initial. [...] Hence Ingush has both stress (fixed initial) and tone (high vs. lack of tone). Distinctive high tone appears only on unstressed syllables.
tone_statements.locator: section 3 'Tone system', opening paragraph after the Kodzasov comparison, and the paragraph following the 'jaazdar=ii' example
tone_statements.summary: Fixed initial stress + privative high (falling) tone lexically specified on a small set of grammatical suffixes/clitics (H vs no tone), realized on unstressed syllables; verb-phrasal rise-fall docks according to the verb form's tone.
